concerns.text: T021 implements the Yeo 7-network atlas for DMN extraction. This violates Constitution Principle VI ('ROI extraction MUST use the AAL atlas') and contradicts the Plan's explicit architectural decision to use AAL. The task silently weakens the constitutional constraint by implementing the Spec's FR-003 (Yeo) instead of the Constitution/Plan mandate (AAL).

T012b enforces strict filtering for 'mindfulness intervention metadata' and T050 raises DataFetchError on failure. This violates the Plan's 'Dataset Scarcity Contingency' which explicitly allows proceeding with 'any available resting-state dataset' if <3 mindfulness datasets are found. The task blocks the plan's fallback mechanism, risking pipeline failure when ideal data is scarce.

T015 (motion exclusion filter) is unchecked/missing. This leaves FR-006 ('System MUST exclude subjects with head motion >3mm...') and SC-004 without an implementing task, violating the requirement to preserve the motion artifact control constraint.

T013 (fMRIPrep Docker runner) and T016 (Nilearn fallback) are unchecked/missing. This leaves FR-002 (standardized preprocessing) and the Plan's compute feasibility strategy (fallback to Nilearn) without executable code, violating the requirement to preserve the preprocessing constraint.

T007 defines `atlas_choice` as 'Yeo' in the config. This contradicts Constitution Principle VI and the Plan's mandate to use the AAL atlas, creating a configuration-level constraint violation that will cause runtime errors if the Plan's atlas choice is intended to override the Spec.
